reason: The narrative demonstrates clear collaboration between leadership and people. Deborah, the judge and prophetess, summons Barak to lead a military campaign. Barak, in turn, mobilizes the people ('וַיַּזְעֵק בָּרָק אֶת־ זְבוּלֻן וְאֶת־ נַפְתָּלִי' - 'Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali'), and 10,000 men from these tribes respond and gather. The leaders and people then work jointly: Deborah accompanies Barak in the military campaign ('וַתַּעַל עִמּוֹ דְּבוֹרָה' - 'Deborah went up with him'), and Barak leads the assembled force down from Mount Tabor in coordinated action against Sisera. The text concludes by noting that 'the hand of the children of Israel was growing harder and harder against Jabin, king of Canaan, until they destroyed him,' indicating sustained cooperative effort between leadership and populace toward a shared military objective.
